His origins are uncertain: Ra ond Osiris are both cited as his father, and his mother may be Nephthys, Hesat, or Bastet. His fully human form is seen only in the temple of Ramses II of Abydos. What is certain is his role as chief embalmer. Name this mysterious Egyptian deity, often depicted with the head of a jackal, who rules the underworld.

He announces to the senator that "the beast with two backs" is being created and observes "we cannot all be masters, nor all masters cannot be truly follow'd." He suspects his plain-spoken wife Emilia is having an affair and thus lusts after Desdemona. For 10 points—name this most villain who is jealous of Michael Cassio's promotion in Othello.

The referendum establishing it was the first time in the country's history that women voted. Vincent Auriol and René Coty were its only presidents, but the weak, compromise cabinets that Félix Gouin's constitution encouraged changed rapidly, and it had twenty-two prime ministers in twelve years of existence. The system's failures became evident during the Algerian crisis, which allowed Charles de Gaulle to return to politics and rewrite the Constitution at will. Name this regime in place from 1946 to 1958 in France.

The iterated version of this problem was examined by Robert Axelrod, who discovered that, when repeated over the long term, selfish strategies tended to hurt the player using them. According to its rules, cooperation between the two players would yield the best net result, but if one player cooperates while the other defects, the player who defects will go free at the expense of his partner. Name this theoretical problem that depicts two individuals being interrogated in separate jail cells.

She became pregnant in an adulterous relationship, and her lover, the king, called her husband home from the war so that the child would appear legitimate. This ploy failed, as her husband refused to stay with her, in comfort, while his men were sleeping in tents. The king then sent her husband, Uriah, to the front lines, where he was killed, so that the king could marry her. Name this woman who was seen on her roof by King David.

On the Third Circuit bench, he was known as "The Fighting Little Judge." In a 1958 gubernatorial primary loss to John Patterson, he refused the support of the Ku Klux Klan and received the endorsement of the NAACP. After winning the Florida primary in 1972, Arthur Bremer shot him while he was campaigning in Laurel, Maryland, leaving him paralyzed. Name this segregationist who ran for president in 1968 on the American Independent Party ticket, the longtime Alabama governor who famously "stood in the schoolhouse doors" to prevent integration of his state's public schools.

Some of his short stories are collected in Constancia and Other Stories for Virgins. He fictionalized the conquista in "All Cats Are Gray." This author edited his country's "Review of Literature" until 1958, and his other critical works include "The New Hispano-American Novel" and Don Quixote, or the Critique of Reading, but he is probably best known for his novels, the first of which was 1958's Where the Air Is Clear. Identify the Mexican diplomat and author of Terra Nostra, The Old Gringo, and The Death of Artemio Cruz.

Following the allocations at the Congress of Vienna, it became the fourth largest German-speaking state in Europe. It was made the ninth electorate of the Holy Roman Empire after its Duke, Ernest Augustus, arranged a marriage with the daughter of George William and remained independent until it was annexed by Prussia. Because its royal house was descended from Sophia of the Palatinate, granddaughter of England's James I, its king George Louis was invited in 1714 to become George I of England. Name this German kingdom which thus established a namesake British royal house.

One was known for his sacred axe, or Parashu, which lopped off one of Ganesh's tusks. Another one, Naram-Sin, was a half-man, half-lion. The final one, Khalki, will appear on a white horse to destroy the world. Better- known ones include the husband of Sita, the charioteer in the Mahabarata, and the Buddha. These are all what Earthly manifestations of Vishnu?

When he died, he bequeathed a large sum of money to the support of "decaying artists." He was only fifteen when the Royal Academy exhibited one of his watercolors; later they showed his first oil painting, Fishermen at Sea. His classically inspired paintings include Dido Building Carthage and Ulysses Deriding Polyphemus, though he is also known for stormy scenes like The Evening of the Deluge. Name this English painter of The Slave Ship and Rain, Steam, and Speed.

In this book, an older woman and her young maid try to escape the traditional experience of their fellow travelers by meeting the local residents. They have lunch with a doctor at the Marabar Caves and become embroiled in a court case when Miss Quested accuses the doctor of rape. This case brings to the forefront the racial tensions between the natives and the ruling English. Name this novel centering around Mrs. Moore, Dr. Aziz, and Fielding, written by E.M. Forster.

The Supreme Court upheld it in Ableman v. Booth, voiding Wisconsin's "personal liberty law" as contravening federal authority. Those charged under it were not entitled to a jury and could not testify in their own defense, and it authorized a network of "special commissioners" who could impose fines at will. Name this part of the Compromise of 1850 which, zealously enforcing Constitutional Article IV, Section 2, mandated the return of those who escaped northward.

This co-founder of the liberal Fortschritspartei, which opposed Bismarck, accompanied Heinrich Schliemann on an excavation of Troy. He proved that phlebitis is not the cause of diseases and coined the terms "thrombosis" and "embolism." name this German polymath who popularized the idea that cells arise from other cells.

The party he founded rebelled against him over the Lavon Affair, causing him to resign from office and spend his latter political life as head of the opposition Rafi party. Earlier, he had created the powerful Histadrut labor confederation and the Mapai party, which eventually became a founding partner of Labor. Always serving as his own defense minister, he suffered a brief interregnum at the hands of Moshe Sharett but otherwise, who was the prime minister of Israel from the state's 1948 founding to 1963?

She established herself with roles in A Price Above Rubies and as Meryl Streep's daughter in One True Thing. The National Board of Review named her the Breakthrough Star of 1996, and she became a Golden Globe winner for 2000's Nurse Betty. Yet, her box office draw wasn't established until she put on weight for a role as a Helen Fielding character. Who is this actress best known for her roles as Roxie in Chicago and as the title character in Bridget Jones' Diary?

The Robinson-Patman Act outlawed the use of this practice for anti-competitive purposes. Examples of the first degree type include allowing for bargaining or issuing coupons; examples of the second degree include selling products cheaper in bulk portions, and examples of the third degree include offering discounts for children or seniors. Name this practice where businesses charge varying prices for the same product.

The son of Zachary, a priest in the course of Abia who lost and then regained the ability to speak, he grew up in the small town of Ain-Karim. His mother, Elizabeth, was the daughter of Aaron, and his second cousin, via Matham, was Mary. Though some observers commented that he "hath a devil" for his manic preaching and desert-influenced countenance, he sought to purify the bodies of those whose souls were cleansed by his sermons. Name this Biblical figure whose head was removed at the behest of Salome.

He lambasted the attempt to seize Rip Van Dam's salary, helped found the Popular Party, and opposed the "hatchetman" Francis Harison. His first two lawyers were disbarred by the presiding judge, James Delancy, for attempting to defend him. He then hired Andrew Hamilton, who shocked the court by declining to contest authorship of the New York Weekly Journal's attacks on governor William Cosby. Name this colonial publisher whose trial established that truth is an absolute defense to libel.

Fulfilling the discovered task, the characters in this play sing songs about execution and otherwise attempt to annoy each other. Characters include the misogynist Garcin, the seductress Inez, and the adulterous murderer Estrelle. Name this drama, concluding that "Hell is other people," written by Jean-Paul Sartre.

Actual infections of the agent that produces it are incredibly rare, as it is produced by an anaerobe of the genus Clostridium. It blocks acetylcholine release from neurons, causing flaccid paralysis, and thus, beginning in 1989, patients suffering from blepharospasm and strabismus, characterized by excessive muscle contractions, were prescribed it as treatment. Name this compound often associated with food poisoning, which some people inject to reduce wrinkles around the eyes.

At this battle, Aristides succeeded in winning Psyttaleia, and, according to Herodotus, one side took especially heavy losses because its soldiers could not swim. Name this naval battle of 480 BC, which saw Greek forces of Eurybiades and Themistocles defeat the Persians under Xerxes I.

Dissenting justice John McLean cited a provision in the Northwest Ordinance as a valid precedent for the law overturned in the majority decision of this case. Benjamin Curtis, who also dissented, claimed that the decision ignored citizenship rights granted by the Articles of Confederation. Nonetheless, the majority opinion, delivered by Chief Justice Taney (TAW-nee), declared the Missouri Compromise unconstitutional and rejected the argument that entering a free state annuls any relationship of slavery. Name this 1857 case in which a slave unsuccessfully sued for his freedom.

A speculated third type of these is caused by carbon detonation and leaves no remnant, and the energies they release are often measured in the unit foe. The emission of nickel-56 is characteristic of the first type of these, which are probably caused by dwarves that have acquired mass in excess of the Chandrasekhar limit. The core of the most common type of these, type II, is comprised of iron-56 because that nuclide has the highest binding energy per nucleon, and thus is the terminus of stellar nucelosynthesis. Identify these violent explosions of massive stars.

In a clash at Panipat, he defeated Mahmud Tughluq, allowing him to raze Delhi. Victory over Tokhtamysh on the Kur River allowed his troops to occupy Moscow; by that time, he had also overrun Persia, Iraq, and the Caspian coast. Both Egypt and Byzantium prepared to surrender after he defeated the Ottomans in battle, but he died at Otrar during an expedition against China. His son Rokh buried him in the mausoleum of Gur-e Amir and briefly reunited his lands, and further descendents established the Mughal dynasty. Name this Samarkand-based conqueror, known for his paralyzed right side.

This city was the setting of an artistic contest involving the depiction of the sacrifice of Isaac. Lorenzo Ghiberti won it, and earned the right to design the bronze doors for its bapistry, while rival Filippo Brunelleschi went on to design the dome for its cathedral, Santa Maria del Fiore. Name this city, also the home of the Uffizi, which exhibits the many works commissioned by the Medicis.

Early in his career he served with John Hawkins on a slave ship, until one voyage, where their ship was damaged by a hurricane and then ransacked by Spaniards at Vera Cruz. He responded by bombarding and raiding several cities in Panama. Nicknamed "The Dragon" by his Spanish rivals, he was knighted by Elizabeth I and accomplished his most famous feat aboard his vessel, the Golden Hind. Name this first English explorer to circumnavigate the globe.

He reveals his true identity to Prince Uttar and protects him, winning the favor of King Virata and securing Virata's daughter for his son Abhimanyu. He kills his rival Karna in war and uses his skill as the greatest archer in the world to win the hand of the princess Draupadi, whom his mother Kunti tells him to share with his four brothers. Name this Pandava brother, the hero of the Mahabharata to whom Krishna enunciates the Bhagavad-Gita.

Its second section addressed the practices of hotels, restaurants, and theaters and was quickly upheld by the Supreme Court in the Heart of Atlanta Motel test case. More expected were Title 7, dealing with businesses that have more than fifteen employees, and Title 1, enforcing the 15th and 24th Amendments. Bob Dole voted for, but Al Gore Sr. And Robert Byrd voted against, what landmark 1964 bill to end segregation and expand the exercise of voting rights?
